A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Wavelet Canonical Coherence for Nonstationary Signals. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 and Appendices C–E report original simulation results and analyses of hippocampal LFP recordings, including permutation tests and lagged coherence estimates.

after.justification: The original simulations and LFP analyses remain, with an additional LSP comparison on the LFP data in Table 2.

M1.justification: The WaveCanCoh and Causal-WaveCanCoh definitions, spectral estimation, eigendecomposition and Algorithms 1–2 are retained. The newly stated Haar-wavelet choice for LFP analysis documents an existing implementation without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the MvLSW and AR(2)-mixture simulations and the same rat Mitt LFP recordings for correct-versus-incorrect memory decisions. The added LSP comparison uses existing data and task coverage.

E2.justification: LSP was already evaluated against WaveCanCoh in the AR(2) simulation. V2 additionally evaluates it in the LFP comparison in Section 6 and Table 2, where v1 reported only WaveCanCoh results.

E3.justification: The reported simulation dimensions and lengths, LFP sampling rate, 40 correct and 32 incorrect trials, scales, selected times and 0.2-second windows remain unchanged. The new LSP comparison explicitly uses the same data and permutation-test procedure.

E4.justification: The AR(2) test outside the MvLSW assumptions and the existing scale-specific and lead-lag analyses are retained. No new ablation, sensitivity sweep or robustness scenario is introduced; the added LSP table is a comparator evaluation.

E5.justification: Both versions report 1000 MvLSW replicates, 500 AR(2) replicates, 95% Wald confidence intervals and 1000 permutations for the LFP tests. Table 2 extends the existing significance-reporting practice to LSP without changing the statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds LSP coherence differences and p-values, including 0.008 with p = 0.999 at scale 5 and 0.5 seconds. Figure 3 replaces the displayed canonical-vector trajectories under the retained simulation description. Appendix C newly reports runtime observations. All numerical entries in WaveCanCoh Table 1 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds asymptotic time and storage complexity comparisons with standard CCA, including O(JTd^3) total time for P approximately equal to Q = d. The coherence definitions and Appendix B eigenvalue and consistency proofs are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: time-varying scale-specific coherence, theoretically supported estimation, channel contributions and behaviorally relevant LFP findings. Additional comparisons support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: V2 suggests that smoothing explains LSP's limited sensitivity in the new LFP comparison. Appendix F expands v1's brief fixed-scale limitation with sampling-rate considerations, time-frequency tradeoffs, downsampling guidance and possible adaptive-wavelet extensions.

D1.justification: V2 specifies Haar wavelets for LFP analysis and reports an Apple Mac with 16 GB RAM and a six-core CPU, simulations within 2.5 seconds per replicate and all results within three hours. It also states that supplementary code is provided and the real dataset is not public. Both versions already identify the same code repository.

R1.justification: V2 adds five references, including Bruns, Chang and Glover, Ghuman and colleagues, Hargreaves and colleagues, and Skidmore and colleagues. The introduction briefly distinguishes existing pairwise or within-network wavelet connectivity work from the proposed between-group framework; the central novelty claim remains.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording and terminology corrections, expands Sections 1 and 6, adds computational discussion and a dedicated limitations appendix, and includes acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 moves from Appendix D.3 to Section 6, and Table 2 is added beside it. Figure 3 is redrawn with different axis ranges, several figures receive sizing or label adjustments, and the title-page author layout is compressed. The overall visual organization is retained.

improvement.justification: The added LFP comparator in Table 2 provides a useful reference missing from v1. Computational requirements and data-access limitations are clearer, and Appendix F develops the earlier brief limitation into practical guidance. These improve validation and transparency, while the core method and most empirical evidence remain unchanged.
